'''Frank Wilcoxon''' (2 September 1892 – 18 November 1965) was a [[chemist]] and [[statistician]], known for the development of several [[Statistical hypothesis testing|statistical tests]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bradley|first1=Ralph A.|last2=Hollander|first2=Myles|author2-link=Myles Hollander|editor1-last=Johnson|editor1-first=Norman L.|editor2-last=Kotz|editor2-first=Samuel|title=Leading Personalities in Statistical Sciences: From the Seventeenth Century to the Present|date=1997|publisher=Wiley-Interscience|isbn=0471163813|pages=372–375|chapter=Wilcoxon, Frank}}<!--|accessdate=28 July 2014--></ref>

== Education and career ==
Frank Wilcoxon was born to American parents on September 2nd 1892 in [[County Cork]], [[History of Ireland (1801–1923)|Ireland]].<ref name="biometrics1966">Bradley, R.A. (1966) ''Obituary: Frank Wilcoxon.'' Biometrics 22(1): 192–194</ref> He grew up in [[Catskill (town), New York|Catskill, New York]], but received part of his education in England. In 1917, he graduated from [[Pennsylvania Military College]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] After the [[First World War]], he entered graduate studies, first at [[Rutgers University]], where he was awarded an [[Master's degree|M.S.]] in [[chemistry]] in 1921, and then at [[Cornell University]], where he obtained a [[Phd]] in [[physical chemistry]] in 1924.

Wilcoxon entered a research career, working at the [[Boyce Thompson Institute]] for Plant Research from 1925 to 1941. He then moved to the [[Atlas Powder Company]], where he designed and directed the Control Laboratory, before joining the [[American Cyanamid|American Cyanamid Company]] in 1943. During this time, he developed an interest in inferential statistics through the study of [[Ronald Fisher]]'s 1925 text, ''[[Statistical Methods for Research Workers]]''. He retired in 1957 and died on 18 November 1965.

== Research ==
Over his career, Wilcoxon published over 70 papers.<ref name="biometrics1967">Karas, J. & Savage, I.R. (1967) ''Publications of Frank Wilcoxon (1892–1965).'' Biometrics 23(1): 1–10</ref> His best-known paper<ref name="biometrics1945">Wilcoxon, F. (1945) ''Individual Comparisons by Ranking Methods.'' Biometrics Bulletin 1: 80–83.</ref> contained the two new statistical tests that still bear his name, the [[Mann–Whitney U|Wilcoxon rank-sum test]] and the [[Wilcoxon signed-rank test]]. These are [[non-parametric]] alternatives to the unpaired and paired [[Student's t-test|Student's ''t''-test]]s, respectively.
